SELECTED_INDEX: 8
CONFIDENCE: 0.27
EXPLANATION: The spectrum shows the typical NO₂ Raman pattern: a strong ν_s(NO₂) band at 1378 cm⁻¹ together with accompanying deformation/rocking modes near 830 cm⁻¹ (837 cm⁻¹) and 700 cm⁻¹. Among the ten candidates only molecule 8 (C/C=C\C(=NC)[N+](=O)[O-]) contains a nitro group, so it alone can account for this triad of peaks. The intense 1644 cm⁻¹ line is readily assigned to the C=N stretch of the imine function present in 8, while the medium band at 1243 cm⁻¹ fits the C–N stretch. Aliphatic and vinylic C–H stretches observed between 2923–3056 cm⁻¹ are also consistent with the hydrocarbon framework of 8. No other candidate offers a coherent explanation for the NO₂-specific bands, making candidate 8 the most plausible match.
